name: Concession Tapering (Diminishing Return Signaling)
scenario: Commercial contract dispute over licensing fee reductions.
script: "In our initial review, we conceded $25,000 to reach $200,000. In our second revision, we stretched to concede $10,000 down to $190,000. Today, we can make an absolute final adjustment of $2,500 to $187,500, but our operational margins are completely exhausted."
defense: Name the schedule: diminishing adjustments are internal pricing, not our ceiling; our limit is $170,000, not $187,500.
originFull: The Rescorla-Wagner Learning Model and Expectation Formation show that successively smaller concession steps signal that the bargainer is approaching their hard reservation boundary.
defenseFull: Reject the psychological tapering signal: "Your diminishing adjustments reflect an internal pricing schedule, not our economic ceiling. We cannot execute at $187,500; our commercial limit is $170,000 regardless of the pacing of your previous increments."
